ratings_why.fun: Reading the shop as a menu of texts makes every Recruit Phase a real choice, and the payoffs grow wearers steadily, but the tribe's own stats are thin and the Tier 1 wearers fade late.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because the shop itself becomes the tribe's text pool and a worn unit's tribe counts for other tribes' cards, so the board changes shape every game in a way no current tribe touches.

verdict_why: The engine is sound, but three rules questions (Bettie's count, worn Start of Combat timing, Tam wearing a Changeling) need answers before it can be played.

points.text: Say whether Wicker Moll's Stocks and Inside-Out Tod's sale-wears count as guises put on for Bettie Underhill. As written, every buy-and-sell under Tod adds a Bettie stack with no limit.
Hoverfly Guest and Penny Second gain the enemy's text at Start of Combat. Say whether a worn Start of Combat effect fires that same fight.
When Tam Twice wears one of your own Changelings, say whether it also takes that unit's guises (for example Grandfer Acorn's three).
Adopt the designer's fallback (units of shop tier minus two are always wearable) so Cradle Foundling and Ant-Nest Grub keep a job late and the Porter isn't a must-buy.

standouts.why: Wicker Moll turns every guise into a second copy of the text for 1 gold, a clear Tier 5 direction card.
Tam Twice copying your own carry is the climber's dream: one strong text, twice.
Grandfer Acorn stacking three guises is a capstone-feeling Tier 5 that rewards planning the shop.

weakest.why: Pip Unlike's mirror usually makes a worn text worse, and the four swaps are hard to read on one card.
Cradle Foundling can wear only Tier 1 units, which barely show up past Tier 3.
Coat-Peg Steward is fight-only, needs your Changelings to die first, and sits under the Tier 5 in-fight target.

flags.note: Inside-Out Tod's sale-wear has no once-a-turn limit, so buy-and-sell turns gold straight into stats, and more so with Bettie.
A 1-gold 3/6 Stock with up to Tier 5 text beats buying the original most of the time.
The Lady's golden text also reaches Moll's Stocks, and her golden doubles worn numbers again, a very high roll.
Penny Second wipes up to four front-row texts; counterplay is moving carries to the back row, worth the owner's eye.
Unclear whether the worn enemy's Start of Combat text fires that fight.
Unclear whether Stock wears and Tod's sale-wears count as guises put on.
